solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pith helmet: most superior one

parts.note: top means highest or best of all
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A colonial-style hat rated as the very best one available.
explanation.walkthrough: A topi (or topee) is a lightweight sun helmet made from pith, worn in hot climates.
explanation.definitionFit: Topi is the Anglo-Indian name for the lightweight sun hat made of dried pith.

clue.text: Casual worker delayed making model

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: A temporary employee turned up late, which ended up becoming a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or exemplar to be copied, which is a sense of model.

clue.text: Pale 1950's youth sought by police?

parts.note: wan means pallid or sickly-looking
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a British youth of the 1950s with Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A pallid young Teddy boy of the fifties is being hunted by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth subculture known for drape jackets and quiffs; the question mark marks the definition as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect the police are hunting is described as wanted, as on a poster.

clue.text: Flee from snakes initially invading European headland

indicators.note: invading means this letter pushes its way into the middle of the European headland

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word snakes

parts.note: the first letter of snakes

explanation.surface: Someone runs away when snakes overrun a promontory somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to get away from danger or captivity, a synonym of flee.

clue.text: One who makes an impression as a craftsman

definitions.text: One who makes an impression as a craftsman

parts.words: One who makes an impression as a craftsman
parts.note: reads as someone who impresses people, but a craftsman making an impression literally cuts an image into a metal plate

explanation.walkthrough: Making an impression usually means impressing people; here it is literal, cutting lines into metal for printing.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher incises designs into metal plates with acid, producing printed impressions as a craft.

clue.text: Sound reason for corvine cries

indicators.note: sound tells us to take a word that is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: a cause is a reason for something

explanation.surface: A good explanation for why crows make their noises.
explanation.walkthrough: Corvine means relating to crows; the clue looks like it asks for a sound reason, i.e. a valid one.
explanation.definitionFit: Crows and rooks make harsh calls known as caws.

clue.text: Quiet, skilled workman, one devoted to a cause

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A softly spoken craftsman who is also a committed activist.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter or adherent of a party or cause.

clue.text: Old bloke extremely negligent about a new contract

parts.note: cove is old-fashioned British slang for a man or chap

indicators.note: about means those outer letters go around the next pieces
extremely asks for only the outermost letters of negligent

parts.note: the first and last letters of negligent
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow, very careless, was concerned with a new agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bloke' looks like an elderly man, but it signals a dated slang word for any man.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement, a kind of contract.

clue.text: Fellow protégé, a pusillanimous type

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
a ward is someone under the protection of a guardian

explanation.surface: A colleague's young charge turns out to be lacking in courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pusillanimous means timid and lacking courage, so such a person is a coward.

clue.text: Communication from police officer's district

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, and the possessive adds S
a patch is the area a person covers

explanation.surface: A message sent from the area a detective is in charge of.
explanation.walkthrough: A patch is the area a police officer or salesperson routinely covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official message or report, a form of communication.

clue.text: Epic tale of silver found in South Africa

indicators.note: found in means silver's symbol sits inside the abbreviation for South Africa

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A long adventure story about a silver discovery in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic narrative, originally Norse, much like an epic.

clue.text: Rent a bar for a change, deviating from type

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of rent and bar are given a new order

explanation.surface: Leasing out a pub as an unusual move, which strays from the normal pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant describes something that departs from what is normal or typical.

clue.text: Small rodent's sleeping-place beside Yorkshire river

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
the Ouse flows through York in northern England

explanation.surface: A little animal's nest lies next to a river in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'; fittingly, the dormouse is famed for sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small, mainly nocturnal rodent known for long hibernation.

clue.text: A specific person finished first we hear

indicators.note: we hear indicates a word that is pronounced the same as the answer

parts.note: to finish first in a race is to have won

explanation.surface: A particular individual came top in the contest, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: One can mean a particular individual, as in 'the one who left early'.

clue.text: Carefully examine old vicar about spoils from robbery

indicators.note: about means the vicar's title is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar
a haul is the loot taken in a theft

explanation.surface: Check closely an elderly clergyman over some stolen loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to inspect it thoroughly and repair it.

clue.text: Setbacks concerning poetic endeavours

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
verses are pieces of poetry

explanation.surface: Problems arising with someone's attempts at poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverses are misfortunes or defeats, much like setbacks.

clue.text: Wild moor originally featuring in literary work

indicators.note: featuring in means this letter appears within the literary work

parts.note: a story is a written narrative

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word moor

parts.note: the first letter of moor

explanation.surface: A wild moorland setting appears in a novel, as in Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather is wild and turbulent, so the adjectives share that sense.

clue.text: Heavenly body giving son a sudden shock

parts.note: taken as written
a turn is a brief fright, as in 'it gave me quite a turn'

explanation.surface: An astronomical object startles somebody's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite a turn' is a British idiom for a nasty fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a ringed planet, a type of celestial object.

clue.text: Leaders of expedition travelling near a volcano

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of these four words spell the volcano

explanation.surface: The heads of an exploring party journey close to an active mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on the east coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Article about unidentified writer

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A piece of journalism concerning an author whose name is not known.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, is printed for an author whose name is unknown.

clue.text: Surpass head of English in south, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters end up arranged in some other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter of English

parts.note: the first letter of English

explanation.surface: Do better than the leader of the English department in the south, in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine someone is to be more brilliant than them, so to excel over them.

clue.text: Shelter in Tyneside street

parts.note: Tyneside, around Newcastle, lies in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A refuge found on a road in Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a bird's home and figuratively any snug refuge or shelter.

clue.text: Bet involving north German composer

indicators.note: involving means the bet wraps around the next letter

parts.note: a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: A gamble that concerns a composer from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle operas.

clue.text: Nobleman's make of car and ship

parts.note: a marque is a brand of vehicle, such as Jaguar
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's brand of motor and his vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquess is a peer ranking above an earl and below a duke.

clue.text: Tightfisted guy ultimately associated with scam

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word guy

parts.note: the last letter of guy

explanation.surface: A miserly fellow who ends up linked to a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means mean or reluctant to spend money, just as tightfisted does.
